verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that users can register and sign in to Entra with passkeys (FIDO2) stored on security keys, native or third-party passkey providers, or Microsoft Authenticator, and that this eliminates passwords. Community reports of a FIDO downgrade attack depend on admins keeping alternative fallback methods. They raise a security caveat but do not show that passwordless sign-in fails to work. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of platform-biometric flows (e.g., Windows Hello), independent hands-on corroboration that passwordless sign-in works as described.

support.subject: As an employee, I can sign in without a password — passwordless flows via passkeys, authenticator, or platform biometrics documented and supported

citations.quote: users in your organization can then register and sign in to their Microsoft Entra account using a passkey stored on a FIDO2 security key, a native or third-party passkey provider, or in Microsoft Authenticator
passkeys (FIDO2) offer a frictionless sign-in experience by eliminating passwords, reducing prompts, and enabling fast, secure authentication across devices
